en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn phrasal verbs for work, people and problems, and where it, him and her go. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: From A2 to B1: work and plans
steps.text: You already know get up, turn off, look for and pick up. Let's add seven phrasal verbs you'll hear at work.
steps.body: Recap: a **phrasal verb** = verb + small word with a **new meaning**, and with **it / them** the small word goes after: turn **it** off. New for **work and plans**: **set up, carry on, put off, call off, look into, fill in, hand in**. Indonesian trap: **diundur** (it happens later) = **put off**, but **batal** (it doesn't happen) = **call off**. And *mengisi formulir* is **fill in** a form (American: **fill out**), not 'fill the form'.

steps.title: At the office
steps.text: Here they are at work. Notice which plans still happen and which don't.
steps.body: **put off** and **carry on** can take a verb with **-ing**: put off **going**, carried on **working**.

examples.en: Can you set up a meeting with the client for Monday?
examples.id: Bisa atur rapat dengan klien untuk hari Senin?

examples.en: We had a short break and then carried on working.
examples.id: Kami istirahat sebentar lalu lanjut bekerja.

examples.en: I always put off going to the dentist.
examples.id: Saya selalu menunda pergi ke dokter gigi.

examples.en: It was raining hard, so they called off the football match.
examples.id: Hujannya deras, jadi pertandingan sepak bolanya dibatalkan.

examples.en: The IT team is looking into the problem with the Wi-Fi.
examples.id: Tim IT sedang memeriksa masalah Wi-Fi-nya.

examples.en: Please fill in this form and hand it in at reception.
examples.id: Tolong isi formulir ini lalu serahkan ke resepsionis.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Read the situation and look for the clue.

question.prompt: Complete: The client is sick today, so we're ___ the meeting until next Tuesday.
question.explanation: **until next Tuesday** = the meeting still happens, just later, so it's **put off** (menunda). **call off** = membatalkan: the meeting wouldn't happen at all. **hand in** = menyerahkan, for a report or a form.

steps.title: People and problems
steps.text: Now ten more: five about people and five about problems.
steps.body: **People:** get on with, look after, look forward to, run into, turn down. **Problems:** break down, run out of, give up, sort out, find out. After **give up** and **look forward to**, a verb takes **-ing**: I gave up **smoking** (not 'gave up to smoke'); I'm looking forward to **meeting** you: this *to* is part of the phrase, not the *to* of *want to go*. In the past, change only the verb: **broke** down, **ran** out of, **gave** up.

steps.title: In real life
steps.text: Here they are in everyday sentences.
steps.body: British vs American: **get on with** = **get along with**; **petrol** = **gas**. *Ketemu* by chance is **run into**; a planned *ketemu* is **meet**.

examples.en: Rina gets on well with her colleagues.
examples.id: Rina akur dengan rekan-rekan kerjanya.

examples.en: Sari looks after her grandmother on weekends.
examples.id: Sari merawat neneknya setiap akhir pekan.

examples.en: I ran into Pak Hasan at the mall yesterday.
examples.id: Kemarin saya kebetulan ketemu Pak Hasan di mal.

examples.en: Dimas turned down the invitation because he was too tired.
examples.id: Dimas menolak undangan itu karena dia terlalu capek.

examples.en: My motorbike broke down on the way to the office.
examples.id: Motor saya mogok di jalan ke kantor.

examples.en: We've run out of rice. Can you buy some?
examples.id: Beras kita habis. Bisa tolong belikan?

examples.en: Can you find out what time the train leaves?
examples.id: Bisa cari tahu jam berapa keretanya berangkat?

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas wants to be healthier.

question.prompt: Complete: Dimas is giving up ___ fried food.
question.explanation: After **give up**, a verb takes **-ing**: giving up **eating**. 'giving up to eat' is the same mistake as 'gave up to smoke', and 'giving up eat' has no -ing.

steps.title: it, him, her: middle or end?
steps.text: One last thing: where do it, them, him and her go?
steps.body: Like turn it off, these take **it / them / him / her in the middle**: set it up, put it off, call it off, fill it in, hand it in, turn it down, sort it out, give it up. These **never split**, the word goes **at the end**: look after her, look into it, get on with him, look forward to it, run into him, run out of it. There's no rule you can see, so learn the two lists. Tricks: the **three-word** ones and the **look** ones never split.

pairs.en: put the meeting off → put it off
fill in the form → fill it in
turn down the offer → turn it down
sort out the problem → sort it out
look after the kids → look after them
run into Budi → run into him
get on with Bu Ani → get on with her
look into the problem → look into it

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: A company in Surabaya offers Budi a job, but he wants to stay in Jakarta with his family. What does he say about the offer?

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Saya akan menolaknya.
question.solution: I'm going to turn it down.
question.explanation: **turn down** = menolak, and with **it** the small word goes after it: turn **it** down. 'turn down it' is the same mistake as 'turn off it'.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Andi is your new colleague. You like working with him, and you never argue.

options: I get on well him with.
I get him on well with.
I get on well with him.
question.explanation: **get on with** never splits: the person goes at the end: get on well **with him**. The three-word phrasal verbs (get on with, look forward to, run out of) always stay together.

steps.title: Flashcards
steps.text: Let's review. Say the meaning, then flip the card.

flashcards.front: break down / run out of / sort out

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here is the whole lesson on one page. Learn the third column too: it shows where it, him and her go.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Everyday phrasal verbs (B1)
artifact.intro: Learn each phrasal verb as a whole. With it / him / her, some split (put it off) and some never split (look after her).
rows: put it off / call it off
fill it in / hand it in
sort it out / find out about it
tips: **put off** = it happens later (until Friday); **call off** = it doesn't happen (money back).
After **give up** and **look forward to**: -ing. gave up **smoking**, looking forward to **meeting** you.
Never split: the **three-word** ones and the **look** ones. In the middle: put **it** off, turn **it** down.

examples.en: We put off the trip until March.
examples.id: Kami mengundur perjalanannya sampai Maret.

examples.en: The form? Fill it in and hand it in today.
examples.id: Formulirnya? Isi lalu serahkan hari ini.

examples.en: The kids? I'm looking after them tonight.
examples.id: Anak-anak? Malam ini saya yang menjaga mereka.

examples.en: We've run out of coffee. Can you buy some?
examples.id: Kopi kita habis. Bisa tolong belikan?

steps.text: Want more practice? This British Council page explains where the thing goes, with two short tests.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu akan belajar phrasal verb untuk kerja, orang dan masalah, dan letak it, him dan her. Yuk, kita mulai pelan-pelan.

steps.title: Dari A2 ke B1: kerja dan rencana
steps.text: Kamu sudah kenal get up, turn off, look for dan pick up. Yuk tambah tujuh phrasal verb yang sering kamu dengar di kantor.
steps.body: Ulasan: **phrasal verb** = kata kerja + kata kecil dengan **arti baru**, dan dengan **it / them** kata kecilnya ditaruh di belakang: turn **it** off. Yang baru untuk **kerja dan rencana**: **set up, carry on, put off, call off, look into, fill in, hand in**. Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: **diundur** (tetap terjadi, tapi nanti) = **put off**, sedangkan **batal** (tidak jadi) = **call off**. Dan *mengisi formulir* adalah **fill in** a form (Amerika: **fill out**), bukan 'fill the form'.

steps.title: Di kantor
steps.text: Ini contohnya di tempat kerja. Perhatikan rencana mana yang tetap jadi dan mana yang tidak.
steps.body: **put off** dan **carry on** bisa diikuti kata kerja dengan **-ing**: put off **going**, carried on **working**.

examples.en: Can you set up a meeting with the client for Monday?
examples.id: Bisa atur rapat dengan klien untuk hari Senin?

examples.en: We had a short break and then carried on working.
examples.id: Kami istirahat sebentar lalu lanjut bekerja.

examples.en: I always put off going to the dentist.
examples.id: Saya selalu menunda pergi ke dokter gigi.

examples.en: It was raining hard, so they called off the football match.
examples.id: Hujannya deras, jadi pertandingan sepak bolanya dibatalkan.

examples.en: The IT team is looking into the problem with the Wi-Fi.
examples.id: Tim IT sedang memeriksa masalah Wi-Fi-nya.

examples.en: Please fill in this form and hand it in at reception.
examples.id: Tolong isi formulir ini lalu serahkan ke resepsionis.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Baca situasinya dan cari petunjuknya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: The client is sick today, so we're ___ the meeting until next Tuesday.
question.explanation: **until next Tuesday** = rapatnya tetap terjadi, hanya nanti, jadi pakai **put off** (menunda). **call off** = membatalkan: rapatnya tidak akan terjadi sama sekali. **hand in** = menyerahkan, untuk laporan atau formulir.

steps.title: Orang dan masalah
steps.text: Sekarang sepuluh lagi: lima tentang orang dan lima tentang masalah.
steps.body: **Orang:** get on with, look after, look forward to, run into, turn down. **Masalah:** break down, run out of, give up, sort out, find out. Setelah **give up** dan **look forward to**, kata kerja pakai **-ing**: I gave up **smoking** (bukan 'gave up to smoke'); I'm looking forward to **meeting** you: *to* di sini bagian dari frasanya, bukan *to* seperti di *want to go*. Untuk bentuk lampau, ubah kata kerjanya saja: **broke** down, **ran** out of, **gave** up.

steps.title: Dalam kehidupan sehari-hari
steps.text: Ini contohnya dalam kalimat sehari-hari.
steps.body: British vs Amerika: **get on with** = **get along with**; **petrol** = **gas**. *Ketemu* tanpa sengaja adalah **run into**; *ketemu* yang sudah direncanakan adalah **meet**.

examples.en: Rina gets on well with her colleagues.
examples.id: Rina akur dengan rekan-rekan kerjanya.

examples.en: Sari looks after her grandmother on weekends.
examples.id: Sari merawat neneknya setiap akhir pekan.

examples.en: I ran into Pak Hasan at the mall yesterday.
examples.id: Kemarin saya kebetulan ketemu Pak Hasan di mal.

examples.en: Dimas turned down the invitation because he was too tired.
examples.id: Dimas menolak undangan itu karena dia terlalu capek.

examples.en: My motorbike broke down on the way to the office.
examples.id: Motor saya mogok di jalan ke kantor.

examples.en: We've run out of rice. Can you buy some?
examples.id: Beras kita habis. Bisa tolong belikan?

examples.en: Can you find out what time the train leaves?
examples.id: Bisa cari tahu jam berapa keretanya berangkat?

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dimas ingin hidup lebih sehat.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Dimas is giving up ___ fried food.
question.explanation: Setelah **give up**, kata kerja pakai **-ing**: giving up **eating**. 'giving up to eat' adalah kesalahan yang sama dengan 'gave up to smoke', dan 'giving up eat' tidak punya -ing.

steps.title: it, him, her: di tengah atau di akhir?
steps.text: Satu hal terakhir: di mana letak it, them, him dan her?
steps.body: Seperti turn it off, kata-kata ini menaruh **it / them / him / her di tengah**: set it up, put it off, call it off, fill it in, hand it in, turn it down, sort it out, give it up. Yang ini **tidak pernah dipisah**, katanya di **akhir**: look after her, look into it, get on with him, look forward to it, run into him, run out of it. Tidak ada aturan yang kelihatan, jadi hafalkan dua daftar ini. Triknya: yang **tiga kata** dan yang diawali **look** tidak pernah dipisah.

pairs.en: put the meeting off → put it off
fill in the form → fill it in
turn down the offer → turn it down
sort out the problem → sort it out
look after the kids → look after them
run into Budi → run into him
get on with Bu Ani → get on with her
look into the problem → look into it

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Sebuah perusahaan di Surabaya menawari Budi pekerjaan, tapi dia ingin tetap di Jakarta bersama keluarganya. Apa yang dia katakan tentang tawaran itu?

question.solution: I'm going to turn it down.
question.explanation: **turn down** = menolak, dan dengan **it** kata kecilnya ditaruh setelah it: turn **it** down. 'turn down it' adalah kesalahan yang sama dengan 'turn off it'.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Andi rekan kerja barumu. Kamu senang bekerja dengannya, dan kalian tidak pernah bertengkar.

options: I get on well him with.
I get him on well with.
I get on well with him.
question.explanation: **get on with** tidak pernah dipisah: orangnya di akhir: get on well **with him**. Phrasal verb tiga kata (get on with, look forward to, run out of) selalu tetap bersama.

steps.title: Kartu hafalan
steps.text: Yuk ulangi. Sebutkan artinya, lalu balik kartunya.

flashcards.front: break down / run out of / sort out

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman. Pelajari juga kolom ketiga: di situ terlihat letak it, him dan her.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Phrasal verb sehari-hari (B1)
artifact.intro: Hafalkan setiap phrasal verb secara utuh. Dengan it / him / her, ada yang dipisah (put it off) dan ada yang tidak pernah dipisah (look after her).
rows: put it off / call it off
fill it in / hand it in
sort it out / find out about it
tips: **put off** = tetap terjadi, tapi nanti (until Friday); **call off** = tidak jadi (uang kembali).
Setelah **give up** dan **look forward to**: -ing. gave up **smoking**, looking forward to **meeting** you.
Tidak pernah dipisah: yang **tiga kata** dan yang diawali **look**. Di tengah: put **it** off, turn **it** down.
